L00001: # [NeurIPS 2024] SpreadsheetBench: Towards Challenging Real World Spreadsheet Manipulation
L00002: 
L00003: [Homepage](https://spreadsheetbench.github.io/) · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14991) · [Data](https://github.com/RUCKBReasoning/SpreadsheetBench/tree/main/data)
L00004: 
L00005: ![overview](images/pipeline.png "The benchmark construction pipeline and OJ-style evaluation of SpreadsheetBench.")
L00006: 
L00007: SpreadsheetBench is a challenging spreadsheet manipulation benchmark that (1) contains 912 questions exclusively derived from real-world scenarios, (2) includes spreadsheet files with tabular data in various formats, (3) features a more reliable evaluation metric akin to online judge platforms.
L00008: 
L00009: ## News
L00010: 
L00011: [2025/12] We are releasing [**SpreadsheetBench Verified**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/KAKA22/SpreadsheetBench/blob/main/spreadsheetbench_verified_400.tar.gz), an expert annotated subset of 400 instances. This benchmark was developed in collaboration with [Shortcut.AI](https://shortcut.ai/) (Fundamental Research Labs).
L00012: 
L00013: [2025/04] We open-source the [complete benchmark](https://github.com/RUCKBReasoning/SpreadsheetBench/blob/main/data/all_data_912.tar.gz), including all 912 questions and related spreadsheet files.
L00014: 
L00015: [2024/09] 🔥 SpreadsheetBench has been accepted at NeurIPS D&B Track 2024 as a spotlight.
L00016: 
L00017: [2024/07] 📑 Our paper was published on [arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14991).
L00018: 
L00019: [2024/06] 📦 We released the code for model inference and evaluation.
L00020: 
L00021: [2024/06] 📊 We released the sample data of SpreadsheetBench.
L00022: 
L00023: ## Overview
L00024: 
L00025: We introduce SpreadsheetBench, a challenging spreadsheet manipulation benchmark exclusively derived from real-world scenarios, designed to immerse current large language models (LLMs) in the actual workflow of spreadsheet users. Unlike existing benchmarks that rely on synthesized queries and simplified spreadsheet files, SpreadsheetBench is built from 912 real questions gathered from online Excel forums, which reflect the intricate needs of users. The associated spreadsheets from the forums contain a variety of tabular data such as multiple tables, non-standard relational tables, and abundant non-textual elements. Furthermore, we propose a more reliable evaluation metric akin to online judge platforms, where multiple spreadsheet files are created as test cases for each instruction, ensuring the evaluation of robust solutions capable of handling spreadsheets with varying values. Our comprehensive evaluation of various LLMs under both single-round and multi-round inference settings reveals a substantial gap between the state-of-the-art (SOTA) models and human performance, highlighting the benchmark's difficulty.
L00026: 
L00027: ## Data Statistics and Comparison
L00028: 
L00029: SpreadsheetBench comprising 912 instructions and 2,729 test cases, with an average of three test cases per instruction. The instructions in our benchmark cover a broad spectrum of spreadsheet manipulation types, including find, extract, sum, highlight, remove, modify, count, delete, calculate, and display. The spreadsheet files in our benchmark contain tabular data with various row size, column size, number of table and table formats.
L00030: 
L00031: ![data_statistic](images/data_statistic.png "")
L00032: 
L00033: Table 1 compares SpreadsheetBench to other spreadsheet manipulation benchmarks. Our questions are sourced exclusively from real-world data and exhibits a higher average word count per instruction. Our spreadsheet files contain multiple sheets with non-standard relational tables and multiple tables within a single sheet. Real-world questions often involve additional explanations within the spreadsheet, a characteristic not present in previous benchmarks. Furthermore, we employ OJ-style evaluation metrics with three test cases per instruction.
L00034: 
L00035: ![comparison](images/comparison.png "")
L00036: 
L00037: ## Experiments
L00038: 
L00039: We evaluate LLMs under two distinct settings: 1. Single Round: In this mode, we present the model with the initial few rows of spreadsheet files within the prompt, allowing for only one inference. 2. Multi-Round: Building on the single-round prompt setting, we incorporate additional prompt that utilizes the ReAct technique and code execution feedback to enhance the accuracy of code solutions produced by LLMs over multi-round conversation.
L00040: 
L00041: ![experiments](images/experiments.png "")
L00042: 
L00043: The results shown in Table 2 indicate that current LLMs and spreadsheet agents are inadequate in managing complex spreadsheet manipulation tasks as required by real-world scenarios. There is a substantial gap between existing LLMs or products and human performance produced by Excel experts, emphasizing the critical need for advancement in LLMs tailored for spreadsheet manipulation.
L00044: 
L00045: ## Dataset Introduction
L00046: 
L00047: The sample data are located in ``data/sample_data_200.tar.gz``, containing two hundred data points in JSONL formats.
L00048: Each data point includes the following five attributes:
L00049: - ``id``: The unique id of the data point.
L00050: - ``instruction``: The question about spreadsheet manipulation.
L00051: - ``spreadsheet_path``: The folder path that stores the test cases.
L00052: - ``instruction_type``: The type of the question (i.e., Cell-Level Manipulation or Sheet-Level Manipulation).
L00053: - ``answer_position``: The cell position where the answer needs to be filled in.
L00054: 
L00055: The ```spreadsheet``` folder contains the corresponding spreadsheet files of the data points. There are two hundred folders in the ```spreadsheet``` folder named as unique ids. In each folder, there are multiple test cases named ```{No.}_{id}_input.xlsx``` and ```{No.}_{id}_answer.xlsx```, represent the input file and answer file, respectively.
L00056: 
L00057: ## Environment Setup
L00058: 
L00059: The environment is used for model inference and evaluation and you can install the requirements with pip:
L00060: ```
L00061: pip install -r requirements.txt
L00062: ```
L00063: 
L00064: The inference process can be performed on **Linux**, **Windows**, and **MacOS**.
L00065: During this process, LLMs generate the code solution for each question, and the code solution is further executed to produce the result spreadsheet files.
L00066: 
L00067: The evaluation process (after model inference) can now be performed on **Linux**, **Windows**, and **MacOS**.
L00068: The `open_spreadsheet.py` script opens all spreadsheet files and forces formula recalculation so that cached cell values are available to `openpyxl`. It supports two backends:
L00069: 
L00070: - **LibreOffice (macOS/Linux/Windows):** Requires [LibreOffice](https://www.libreoffice.org/) 7.5+. Install with `brew install --cask libreoffice` (macOS) or `sudo apt install libreoffice-calc` (Linux). This is the default on non-Windows platforms.
L00071: - **win32com (Windows):** Requires Microsoft Excel and `pywin32` (`pip install pywin32`). This is the default on Windows when Excel is installed.
L00072: 
L00073: The backend is auto-detected, or you can force one with `--backend libreoffice` or `--backend win32com`.
L00074: 
L00075: ## Inference
L00076: 
L00077: ### Code Execution Environment
L00078: 
L00079: First, you need to configure the code execution environment. We use a Docker container to execute the Python code generated by LLMs.
L00080: ```
L00081: cd code_exec_docker
L00082: docker build -t xingyaoww/codeact-execute-api -f Dockerfile.api .
L00083: docker build -t xingyaoww/codeact-executor -f Dockerfile.executor .
L00084: ```
L00085: 
L00086: If you have problem installing pip packages inside the docker container, try add ```--network=host``` when running ```docker build```, or other possible [solutions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28668180/cant-install-pip-packages-inside-a-docker-container-with-ubuntu).
L00087: 
L00088: Then, you need to set up a port and deploy the container.
L00089: ```
L00090: bash start_jupyter_server.sh PORT
L00091: ```
L00092: 
L00093: Now, the code execution environment is ready.
L00094: 
L00095: ### Model Deployment
L00096: 
L00097: Then, you need to deploy your model.
L00098: For OpenAI models, you can directly inference with the following settings.
L00099: For open-source models, you can use the OpenAI compatible server provided by [vLLM](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/serving/openai_compatible_server.html).
L00100: 
L00101: ### Single-round Setting
L00102: 
L00103: Get the inference result in single-round setting:
L00104: ```
L00105: cd inference
L00106: bash scripts/inference_single.sh
L00107: ```
L00108: 
L00109: You need to modify the model, api_key, and base_url parameters in inference_single.sh.
L00110: 
L00111: ### Multi-round Setting
L00112: 
L00113: Get the inference result in multi-round setting (Execution Feedback + 5 Rows):
L00114: ```
L00115: bash scripts/inference_multiple_row_exec.sh
L00116: ```
L00117: 
L00118: Get the inference result in multi-round setting (ReAct + Execution Feedback):
L00119: ```
L00120: bash scripts/inference_multiple_react_exec.sh
L00121: ```
L00122: 
L00123: Get the inference result in multi-round setting (ReAct + Execution Feedback + 5 Rows):
L00124: ```
L00125: bash scripts/inference_multiple_row_react_exec.sh
L00126: ```
L00127: 
L00128: You need to modify the model, api_key, and base_url parameters in the scripts.
L00129: The code solution are saved in the ```inference/output``` folder and the result spreadsheet files are saved in the ```data/sample_data_200/outputs``` folder.
L00130: 
L00131: ## Evaluation
L00132: 
L00133: ### Recalculate Spreadsheet Formulas
L00134: 
L00135: Before evaluating, open all spreadsheet files to force formula recalculation. This step caches computed values so that `openpyxl` can read them:
L00136: ```
L00137: cd evaluation
L00138: python open_spreadsheet.py --dir_path ../data/sample_data_200/spreadsheet/TASK_ID
L00139: ```
L00140: 
L00141: The script auto-detects the backend (LibreOffice on macOS/Linux, win32com on Windows). See [Environment Setup](#environment-setup) for installation instructions.
L00142: 
L00143: ### Run Evaluation
L00144: 
L00145: Using the following script to get the evaluation result:
L00146: ```
L00147: cd evaluation
L00148: bash scripts/evaluation.sh
L00149: ```
L00150: 
L00151: You need to modify the setting (single, multi_react_exec, multi_row_exec, or multi_row_react_exec) and model parameters in evaluation.sh.
L00152:

L00170: ## Maintenance
L00171: 
L00172: RUC KBReasoning group will maintain this benchmark in the long term. We will continue to update the benchmark to fix labelling errors, instructions, or other necessary modifications, and all data will be versioned. We also welcome all contributors interested in our benchmark. If you have any questions or want to extend/augment/build on/contribute to the dataset, feel free to contact us via Github or E-mail (<zeyaoma@ruc.edu.cn>, <zbhmint@bit.edu.cn>).

L00012: def datetime_to_float(dt):
L00013:     excel_start_date = datetime.datetime(1899, 12, 30)
L00014:     delta = dt - excel_start_date
L00015:     return delta.days + delta.seconds / 86400.0
L00016: 
L00017: 
L00018: def transform_value(v):
L00019:     if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
L00020:         v = round(float(v), 2)
L00021:     elif isinstance(v, datetime.time):
L00022:         v = str(v)[:-3]
L00023:     elif isinstance(v, datetime.datetime):
L00024:         v = round(datetime_to_float(v), 0)
L00025:     elif isinstance(v, str):
L00026:         try:
L00027:             v = round(float(v), 2)
L00028:         except ValueError:
L00029:             pass
L00030:     return v
L00031: 
L00032: 
L00033: def compare_cell_value(v1, v2):
L00034: 
L00035:     v1 = transform_value(v1)
L00036:     v2 = transform_value(v2)
L00037:     if (v1 == "" and v2 is None) or (v1 is None and v2 == ""):
L00038:         return True
L00039:     if (v1 == "" and v2 == "") or (v1 is None and v2 is None):
L00040:         return True
L00041:     if type(v1) != type(v2):
L00042:         # print(type(v1), type(v2))
L00043:         return False
L00044:     if v1 == v2:
L00045:         return True
L00046:     else:
L00047:         return False

L00050: def _get_color_rgb(color) -> str:
L00051:     """Extract RGB value from color object, defaulting to '00000000' if not a string."""
L00052:     if color and isinstance(color.rgb, str):
L00053:         return color.rgb
L00054:     return "00000000"
L00055: 
L00056: 
L00057: def _compare_colors(color1, color2) -> bool:
L00058:     """Compare two colors using only last 6 characters (RGB), ignoring alpha channel."""
L00059:     rgb1 = _get_color_rgb(color1)
L00060:     rgb2 = _get_color_rgb(color2)
L00061:     return rgb1[-6:] == rgb2[-6:]
L00062: 
L00063: 
L00064: def compare_fill_color(fill1, fill2) -> bool:
L00065:     """Compare fill colors between two cells."""
L00066:     return _compare_colors(fill1.fgColor, fill2.fgColor) and _compare_colors(
L00067:         fill1.bgColor, fill2.bgColor
L00068:     )
L00069: 
L00070: 
L00071: def compare_font_color(font_gt, font_proc) -> bool:
L00072:     """Compare font colors between two cells."""
L00073:     return _compare_colors(font_gt.color, font_proc.color)
L00074:

L00076: def col_num2name(n):
L00077:     """ Convert a column number to an Excel column name """
L00078:     name = ''
L00079:     while n > 0:
L00080:         n, remainder = divmod(n - 1, 26)
L00081:         name = chr(65 + remainder) + name
L00082:     return name
L00083: 
L00084: 
L00085: def col_name2num(name):
L00086:     """ Convert an Excel column name to a column number """
L00087:     num = 0
L00088:     for c in name:
L00089:         num = num * 26 + (ord(c) - ord('A') + 1)
L00090:     return num
L00091: 
L00092: 
L00093: def parse_cell_range(range_str):
L00094:     """ Parse a range string like 'A1:AB12' """
L00095:     start_cell, end_cell = range_str.split(':')
L00096:     start_col, start_row = '', ''
L00097:     for char in start_cell:
L00098:         if char.isdigit():
L00099:             start_row += char
L00100:         else:
L00101:             start_col += char
L00102:     
L00103:     end_col, end_row = '', ''
L00104:     for char in end_cell:
L00105:         if char.isdigit():
L00106:             end_row += char
L00107:         else:
L00108:             end_col += char
L00109: 
L00110:     return (col_name2num(start_col), int(start_row)), (col_name2num(end_col), int(end_row))
L00111: 
L00112: 
L00113: def generate_cell_names(range_str):
L00114:     """ Generate a list of all cell names in the specified range """
L00115:     if ':' not in range_str:
L00116:         return [range_str]
L00117:     (start_col, start_row), (end_col, end_row) = parse_cell_range(range_str)
L00118:     columns = [col_num2name(i) for i in range(start_col, end_col + 1)]
L00119:     cell_names = [f"{col}{row}" for col in columns for row in range(start_row, end_row + 1)]
L00120:     return cell_names
L00121:

L00123: def cell_level_compare(wb_gt, wb_proc, sheet_name, cell_range):
L00124:     if sheet_name not in wb_proc:
L00125:         return False, "worksheet not found"
L00126:     ws_gt = wb_gt[sheet_name]
L00127:     ws_proc = wb_proc[sheet_name]
L00128: 
L00129:     cell_names = generate_cell_names(cell_range)
L00130: 
L00131:     for cell_name in cell_names:
L00132:         cell_gt = ws_gt[cell_name]
L00133:         cell_proc = ws_proc[cell_name]
L00134: 
L00135:         if not compare_cell_value(cell_gt.value, cell_proc.value):
L00136:             msg = f"Value difference at cell {cell_gt.coordinate}: ws_gt has {cell_gt.value},\
L00137:                     ws_proc has {cell_proc.value}"
L00138:             return False, msg
L00139:         
L00140:         # if not compare_fill_color(cell_gt.fill, cell_proc.fill):
L00141:         #     msg = f"Fill color difference at cell {cell_gt.coordinate}: ws_gt has {cell_gt.fill.fgColor.rgb},\
L00142:         #             ws_proc has {cell_proc.fill.fgColor.rgb}"
L00143:         #     return False, msg
L00144: 
L00145:         # if not compare_font_color(cell_gt.font, cell_proc.font):
L00146:         #     # msg = f"Font color difference at cell {cell_gt.coordinate}: ws_gt has {cell_gt.font.color.rgb},\
L00147:         #     #        ws_proc has {cell_proc.font.color.rgb}"
L00148:         #     msg = f"Font color difference at cell {cell_gt.coordinate}"
L00149:         #     return False, msg
L00150: 
L00151:     print("Cell values in the specified range are identical.")
L00152:     return True, ""

L00155: def compare_workbooks(gt_file, proc_file, instruction_type, answer_position):
L00156:     if not os.path.exists(proc_file):
L00157:         return False, "File not exist"
L00158:     # Open workbooks
L00159:     try:
L00160:         wb_gt = openpyxl.load_workbook(filename=gt_file, data_only=True)
L00161:         wb_proc = openpyxl.load_workbook(filename=proc_file, data_only=True)
L00162:     except Exception as e:
L00163:         return False, str(e)
L00164: 
L00165:     # Initialize report
L00166:     result = False
L00167:     msg = ""
L00168: 
L00169:     sheet_cell_ranges = answer_position.split(',')
L00170:     result_list = []
L00171:     msg_list = []
L00172:     for sheet_cell_range in sheet_cell_ranges:
L00173:         if '!' in sheet_cell_range:
L00174:             sheet_name, cell_range = sheet_cell_range.split('!')
L00175:             sheet_name = sheet_name.lstrip("'").rstrip("'")
L00176:         else:
L00177:             sheet_name = wb_gt.sheetnames[0]
L00178:             cell_range = sheet_cell_range
L00179:     
L00180:         # process sheet_name and cell_range
L00181:         sheet_name = sheet_name.lstrip("'").rstrip("'")
L00182:         cell_range = cell_range.lstrip("'").rstrip("'")
L00183: 
L00184:         result, msg = cell_level_compare(wb_gt, wb_proc, sheet_name, cell_range)
L00185:         result_list.append(result)
L00186:         msg_list.append(msg)
L00187: 
L00188:     return all(result_list), ""

L00191: def parse_option():
L00192:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser("command line arguments for evaluation.")
L00193:     
L00194:     parser.add_argument('--model', type=str, default='llama', help='model name')
L00195:     parser.add_argument('--setting', type=str, default='single',
L00196:         help='four setting: single, multi_react_exec, multi_row_exec, multi_row_react_exec')
L00197:     parser.add_argument('--dataset', type=str, default="all_data_912", help='dataset name')
L00198: 
L00199:     opt = parser.parse_args()
L00200: 
L00201:     return opt
L00202:

L00204: def evaluation(opt):
L00205:     dataset_path = os.path.abspath(f'../data/{opt.dataset}')
L00206:     with open(f'{dataset_path}/dataset.json', 'r') as fp:
L00207:         dataset = json.load(fp)
L00208: 
L00209:     eval_results = []
L00210:     for data in tqdm(dataset):
L00211:         test_case_results = []
L00212:         for test_case_idx in range(3):
L00213:             gt_path = f"{dataset_path}/spreadsheet/{data['id']}/{test_case_idx + 1}_{data['id']}_answer.xlsx"
L00214:             proc_path = f"{dataset_path}/spreadsheet/{data['id']}/{test_case_idx + 1}_{data['id']}_input.xlsx"
L00215:             # proc_path = f"{dataset_path}/outputs/{opt.setting}_{opt.model}/{test_case_idx + 1}_{data['id']}_output.xlsx"
L00216:             try:
L00217:                 result, _ = compare_workbooks(gt_path, proc_path, data['instruction_type'], data['answer_position'])
L00218:             except:
L00219:                 result = False
L00220:             test_case_results.append(int(result))
L00221:         soft_restriction = test_case_results.count(1) / len(test_case_results)
L00222:         hard_restriction = 0 if 0 in test_case_results else 1
L00223:         eval_results.append({
L00224:             'id': data['id'],
L00225:             'instruction_type': data['instruction_type'],
L00226:             'test_case_results': test_case_results,
L00227:             'soft_restriction': soft_restriction,
L00228:             'hard_restriction': hard_restriction,
L00229:         })
L00230:     
L00231:     with open(f'../outputs/eval_{opt.setting}_{opt.model}.json', 'w') as fp:
L00232:         json.dump(eval_results, fp, indent=4)
L00233: 
L00234: 
L00235: if __name__ == "__main__":
L00236:     opt = parse_option()
L00237:     print(opt)
L00238: 
L00239:     evaluation(opt)

L00001: """
L00002: Open and recalculate spreadsheet files so that formula values are cached,
L00003: enabling openpyxl to read computed values with data_only=True.
L00004: 
L00005: Cross-platform: uses LibreOffice (macOS/Linux) or win32com+Excel (Windows).
L00006: 
L00007: Usage:
L00008:     python open_spreadsheet.py --dir_path /path/to/spreadsheets
L00009: 
L00010:     # To force a specific backend:
L00011:     python open_spreadsheet.py --dir_path /path/to/spreadsheets --backend libreoffice
L00012:     python open_spreadsheet.py --dir_path /path/to/spreadsheets --backend win32com
L00013: 
L00014:     # To specify a custom LibreOffice path:
L00015:     python open_spreadsheet.py --dir_path /path/to/spreadsheets --soffice /path/to/soffice
L00016: 
L00017: Requirements (one of):
L00018:     - LibreOffice 7.5+ (macOS: brew install --cask libreoffice, Linux: apt install libreoffice-calc)
L00019:     - Windows with Microsoft Excel and pywin32 installed (pip install pywin32)
L00020: """
L00021: 
L00022: import os
L00023: import sys
L00024: import shutil
L00025: import argparse
L00026: import subprocess
L00027: import tempfile
L00028: import platform

L00030: 
L00031: # ---- LibreOffice backend (macOS / Linux / Windows) ----
L00032: 
L00033: def find_libreoffice():
L00034:     """Locate the LibreOffice binary."""
L00035:     candidates = [
L00036:         "libreoffice",
L00037:         "soffice",
L00038:         "/Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice",  # macOS
L00039:     ]
L00040:     for candidate in candidates:
L00041:         path = shutil.which(candidate)
L00042:         if path:
L00043:             return path
L00044:         if os.path.isfile(candidate):
L00045:             return candidate
L00046:     return None
L00047: 
L00048: 
L00049: def just_open_libreoffice(filename, soffice_path):
L00050:     """
L00051:     Open an xlsx/xls file in LibreOffice Calc headlessly, which triggers
L00052:     formula recalculation, then save it back as xlsx so that openpyxl
L00053:     can read the cached computed values with data_only=True.
L00054:     """
L00055:     filename = os.path.abspath(filename)
L00056:     if not os.path.isfile(filename):
L00057:         print(f"File not found: {filename}")
L00058:         return False
L00059: 
L00060:     original_dir = os.path.dirname(filename)
